theory.title: Components & JSX
theory.content:
Functional Components

Modern React uses plain functions that accept props and return JSX. They are the recommended approach and support all React features via hooks.

theory.title: useState & useReducer
theory.content:
useState

Adds local state to a component. State updates trigger a re-render. The setter can take a value or an updater function.

function Counter() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  const [text, setText] = useState('');

  // Use updater function when new state depends on previous state
  const increment = () => setCount(prev => prev + 1);

  return (
    <>
      
       setText(e.target.value)} />
    
  );
}

State Update Batching

React batches multiple state updates in event handlers into a single re-render (React 18+ batches everywhere including setTimeout and promises).

// Only ONE re-render despite two setters
function handleClick() {
  setCount(c => c + 1);
  setName('Alice');
}

useReducer

Preferred for complex state with multiple sub-values or when next state depends on previous state in non-trivial ways.

type Action = { type: 'increment' } | { type: 'reset' } | { type: 'set'; value: number };

function reducer(state: number, action: Action): number {
  switch (action.type) {
    case 'increment': return state + 1;
    case 'reset': return 0;
    case 'set': return action.value;
  }
}

const [count, dispatch] = useReducer(reducer, 0);
dispatch({ type: 'increment' });
dispatch({ type: 'set', value: 10 });

theory.title: useEffect & Side Effects
theory.content:
When useEffect Runs

useEffect runs after every render by default. The dependency array controls when it re-runs.

// Runs after every render
useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count}`; });

// Runs once on mount
useEffect(() => { fetchData(); }, []);

// Runs when `userId` changes
useEffect(() => { fetchUser(userId); }, [userId]);

Cleanup

Return a cleanup function to cancel subscriptions, timers, or abort requests when the component unmounts or before the effect re-runs.

useEffect(() => {
  const controller = new AbortController();

  fetch(`/api/users/${userId}`, { signal: controller.signal })
    .then(r => r.json())
    .then(setUser)
    .catch(err => {
      if (err.name !== 'AbortError') setError(err);
    });

  return () => controller.abort(); // cancel on userId change or unmount
}, [userId]);

Common Rules

  • Don't lie about dependencies — include everything the effect uses
  • Use useLayoutEffect only for DOM measurements that must happen before paint
  • Prefer custom hooks over large inline effects for reusability
  • React Strict Mode runs effects twice in development to surface cleanup bugs

theory.title: useRef, useMemo & useCallback
theory.content:
useRef

useRef stores a mutable value that persists across renders without causing re-renders when changed. Most commonly used to hold a reference to a DOM node.

function FocusInput() {
  const inputRef = useRef(null);

  return (
    <>
      
      
    
  );
}

// Storing a mutable value without re-render
const timerRef = useRef | null>(null);
timerRef.current = setInterval(tick, 1000);

useMemo

Memoises the result of an expensive computation, recalculating only when dependencies change.

const filteredUsers = useMemo(
  () => users.filter(u => u.active && u.role === selectedRole),
  [users, selectedRole]
);
// Only recomputes when users or selectedRole changes

useCallback

Memoises a function reference, preventing unnecessary re-renders of child components that receive it as a prop.

const handleSubmit = useCallback(
  (data: FormData) => submitForm(data, userId),
  [userId] // new function only when userId changes
);

// Pair with React.memo on child:
const Form = React.memo(({ onSubmit }) => { ... });

 // no re-render when parent re-renders

theory.title: Context API
theory.content:
Why Context?

Context solves prop drilling — passing data through many intermediate components that don't use it. It broadcasts a value to any descendant that subscribes, no matter how deep.

Creating and Providing Context

// ThemeContext.tsx
type Theme = 'light' | 'dark';
interface ThemeContextValue {
  theme: Theme;
  toggle: () => void;
}

const ThemeContext = createContext(null);

export function ThemeProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const [theme, setTheme] = useState('light');
  const toggle = () => setTheme(t => t === 'light' ? 'dark' : 'light');

  return (
    
      {children}
    
  );
}

Consuming Context

// Custom hook for safe consumption
export function useTheme() {
  const ctx = useContext(ThemeContext);
  if (!ctx) throw new Error('useTheme must be used inside ThemeProvider');
  return ctx;
}

// In any descendant component
function DarkModeToggle() {
  const { theme, toggle } = useTheme();
  return ;
}

When NOT to Use Context

  • For high-frequency updates (every keystroke) — causes all subscribers to re-render
  • For server state (use React Query / SWR instead)
  • For complex global state (use Zustand / Redux instead)

theory.title: Performance Optimisation
theory.content:
When Does React Re-Render?

A component re-renders when its state changes, its parent re-renders, or its context value changes. The virtual DOM diff ensures only changed DOM nodes are updated.

React.memo

Wraps a component so it only re-renders when its props change (shallow comparison).

const UserRow = React.memo(function UserRow({ user, onDelete }) {
  console.log('render', user.id);
  return (
    
      {user.name}
      
    
  );
});

// onDelete must be stable (useCallback) for memo to help:
const handleDelete = useCallback((id) => deleteUser(id), []);

Virtualisation for Long Lists

For lists with 100+ items, only render visible rows using a windowing library:

theory.title: Custom Hooks
theory.content:
What Is a Custom Hook?

A custom hook is a function whose name starts with use that calls other hooks. It extracts stateful logic so it can be shared across components without changing their structure.

useFetch Example

function useFetch(url: string) {
  const [data, setData] = useState(null);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
  const [error, setError] = useState(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    let cancelled = false;
    setLoading(true);

    fetch(url)
      .then(r => { if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${r.status}`); return r.json(); })
      .then(d => { if (!cancelled) { setData(d); setLoading(false); } })
      .catch(e => { if (!cancelled) { setError(e); setLoading(false); } });

    return () => { cancelled = true; };
  }, [url]);

  return { data, loading, error };
}

// Usage
const { data: users, loading } = useFetch('/api/users');

useLocalStorage Example

function useLocalStorage(key: string, initialValue: T) {
  const [value, setValue] = useState(() => {
    try {
      const item = localStorage.getItem(key);
      return item ? JSON.parse(item) : initialValue;
    } catch { return initialValue; }
  });

  const setStored = (newValue: T) => {
    setValue(newValue);
    localStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(newValue));
  };

  return [value, setStored] as const;
}

Rules of Hooks

  • Only call hooks at the top level — no conditions or loops
  • Only call hooks from React functions or other custom hooks
  • ESLint plugin eslint-plugin-react-hooks enforces these rules automatically
